items.stem: A model produces a single cash-forecast number for next quarter. The most responsible way to use it is to:

options.text: Treat it as one estimate with uncertainty, cross-checked against judgement and other evidence
options.rationale: Correct: model output supports, not replaces, judgement and should carry uncertainty.

options.text: Accept it as the definitive answer and stop forecasting
options.rationale: A single number ignores uncertainty and context.

items.explanation: Correct: model output supports, not replaces, judgement and should carry uncertainty.

items.stem: Which TWO are governance expectations for using AI in financial reporting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Documented data lineage and quality checks on model inputs
options.rationale: Correct: input data must be controlled and traceable.

options.text: Model validation and an audit trail for outputs
options.rationale: Correct: validation and auditability are core controls.

options.text: Hiding the model from auditors to protect IP
Removing all human review once accuracy is high
options.rationale: Human oversight remains a required control.

items.explanation: Correct: input data must be controlled and traceable.

items.stem: Why is explainability important when AI informs a lending or budgeting decision?

options.text: Decision-makers must understand and challenge the basis of a recommendation, and may be accountable for it
options.rationale: Correct: accountability and oversight require understanding the reasoning.

options.text: Because explainable models are always more accurate
options.rationale: Explainability does not guarantee higher accuracy.

options.text: Because regulators never allow any automated input
options.rationale: Automated inputs are permitted with controls.

options.text: Because it removes the need for data quality

items.explanation: Correct: accountability and oversight require understanding the reasoning.
